title:
RATIO AND PROPORTION,
(SCALE FACTORS)
objective: LO: I can use scale factors to find missing lengths in similar shapes and on maps.

content.text: A scale factor is the number you multiply by to enlarge or reduce a shape. It is the ratio of corresponding lengths between two similar shapes.
Finding it: Scale factor = new length ÷ original length. If SF > 1, the shape is enlarged. If SF < 1, it is reduced.

examples.expr: SF 2 means add 2 to each side
SF for area is same as for length

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: Scale factor = new ÷ original. Multiply any original length by the SF to get the new length.
key_idea.caption: For area: × SF². For volume: × SF³.

modelled_examples.label: Example 1 – finding scale factor
modelled_examples.question: Triangle A has sides 3, 4, 5 cm. Triangle B has sides 9, 12, 15 cm. Find the scale factor.
modelled_examples.explanation: Divide any corresponding pair of sides.

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – finding missing length
modelled_examples.question: Two similar rectangles. First: 5 cm by 8 cm. Second: 15 cm by ? cm.
modelled_examples.explanation: Find the SF from known corresponding sides, then multiply.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – map scale
modelled_examples.question: A map uses scale 1:50,000. A park is 4 cm on the map. Find real length.
modelled_examples.explanation: Multiply the map measurement by the scale factor.

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – area and scale factor
modelled_examples.question: Two similar shapes have SF = 2. Small shape area = 15 cm². Find larger area.
modelled_examples.explanation: Area scales by the square of the linear scale factor.

practice.heading: Area and volume scale factors

questions.expression: Length SF = 3. Area of small = 8 cm². Large area?
Length SF = 2. Volume of small = 10 cm³. Large volume?
Areas: 9 cm² and 81 cm². Length SF?
Volumes: 27 cm³ and 216 cm³. Length SF?
Length SF = 4. Large area = 320 cm². Small area?

items.statement: Scale factor = new length ÷ original length
A scale factor of 2 means add 2 to each length
If the scale factor is &frac{1}{3}, the shape gets bigger

problems.text: Two similar cylinders have heights in ratio 2:5. The smaller has volume 80 cm³. Find the volume of the larger cylinder.
On a map of scale 1:40,000, a lake has area 3.2 cm². Find the real area in m² and km².
